content.topic: building trust between business and consumers

modelEssay.title: Building Trust Between Business and Consumers
modelEssay.content:
In the realm of commerce, trust is the cornerstone of any successful business-consumer relationship. Trust fosters loyalty and drives repeat business, which is essential for economic sustainability.

Firstly, businesses that prioritize trustworthiness are more likely to attract and retain customers. For instance, companies that offer transparent pricing and clear return policies build a reputation for fairness, which in turn encourages consumer confidence. Moreover, when businesses engage in ethical practices and are open about their processes, consumers are more inclined to trust their products and services. This trust is further reinforced when businesses respond promptly and effectively to customer feedback, demonstrating a commitment to quality and customer satisfaction.

In conclusion, trust is the linchpin that holds the business-consumer relationship together. It not only affects the immediate transactions but also paves the way for long-term partnerships. As such, it is imperative for businesses to invest in building and maintaining trust with their consumers.

structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：总结信任对商业和消费者关系的长远影响，并强调企业建立信任的重要性

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 段落1。

transcript.text: Many people enjoy secret codes.
transcript.translation: 许多人喜欢密码。

transcript.text: The harder the code, the more some people will try to figure it out.
transcript.translation: 密码越难，有些人就越想破解它。

transcript.text: In wartime, codes are especially important.
transcript.translation: 在战时，密码尤为重要。

transcript.text: They help armies send news about battles and the size of enemy forces.
transcript.translation: 它们帮助军队传递关于战斗和敌军规模的消息。

transcript.text: Neither side wants its code broken by the other.
transcript.translation: 任何一方都不希望己方密码被对方破解。

transcript.text: One very important code was never broken.
transcript.translation: 有一个非常重要的密码从未被破解。

transcript.text: It was used during World War II by the Americans.
transcript.translation: 它在第二次世界大战期间被美国人使用。

transcript.text: It was a spoken code, never written down.
transcript.translation: 它是一种口头密码，从未被记录下来。

transcript.text: And it was developed and used by Navajo Indians.
transcript.translation: 并且它是由纳瓦霍印第安人开发和使用的。

transcript.text: They were called the Navajo Code Talkers.
transcript.translation: 他们被称为纳瓦霍密码通信兵。

transcript.text: The Navajos created the code in their own language.
transcript.translation: 纳瓦霍人用自己的语言创造了这种密码。

transcript.text: Navajo is hard to learn, and only a few people know it.
transcript.translation: 纳瓦霍语很难学，只有少数人会说。

transcript.text: So it was pretty certain that the enemy would not be able to understand the Code Talkers.
transcript.translation: 因此可以相当肯定，敌人无法理解密码通信兵的话。

transcript.text: In addition, the Talkers used code words.
transcript.translation: 此外，通信兵们还使用密码词。

transcript.text: They called a submarine an iron fish, and a small bomb thrown by hand a potato.
transcript.translation: 他们称潜艇为‘铁鱼’，称手掷的小炸弹为‘土豆’。

transcript.text: If they wanted to spell something, they used code words for letters of the alphabet.
transcript.translation: 如果想拼写什么，他们就用字母表的代码词。

transcript.text: For instance, the letter A was ant or apple or axe.
transcript.translation: 例如，字母A是‘蚂蚁’、‘苹果’或‘斧头’。

transcript.text: The Code Talkers worked mostly in the islands in the Pacific.
transcript.translation: 密码通信兵主要在太平洋的岛屿上工作。

transcript.text: One or two would be assigned to a group of soldiers.
transcript.translation: 一到两名会被分配到一个士兵小组。

transcript.text: They would send messages by field telephone to the Code Talker in the next group.
transcript.translation: 他们通过野战电话向下一组的密码通信兵发送消息。

transcript.text: And he would relay the information to his commander.
transcript.translation: 然后他再将信息转达给他的指挥官。

transcript.text: The Code Talkers played an important part in several battles.
transcript.translation: 密码通信兵在几场战斗中发挥了重要作用。

transcript.text: They helped troops coordinate their movements and attacks.
transcript.translation: 他们帮助部队协调行动和攻击。

transcript.text: After the war, the U.

transcript.translation: 政府为他们的成就而表彰了他们。

transcript.text: Theirs was the most successful wartime code ever used.
transcript.translation: 他们的密码是有史以来最成功的战时密码。

transcript.text: If you are young and thinking about your career, you'll want to know where you can make a living.
transcript.translation: 如果你还年轻，正在考虑你的职业，你会想知道在哪里可以谋生。

transcript.text: Well, there's going to be a technological replacement of a lot of knowledge-intensive jobs in the next 20 years, particularly in the two largest sectors of the labor force with professional skills.
transcript.translation: 嗯，在未来20年内，许多知识密集型工作将被技术取代，尤其是在劳动力中拥有专业技能的两个最大领域。

transcript.text: One is teaching, and the other, health care.
transcript.translation: 一个是教学，另一个是医疗保健。

transcript.text: You have so many applications and software and platforms that are going to come in and provide information and service in these two fields.
transcript.translation: 会有如此多的应用程序、软件和平台进入这两个领域，提供信息和服务。

transcript.text: Which means a lot of health care and education sectors will be radically changed, and a lot of jobs will be lost.
transcript.translation: 这意味着许多医疗保健和教育部门将发生根本性变化，许多工作岗位将会丧失。

transcript.text: Now, where will the new jobs be found?
transcript.translation: 那么，新的工作岗位将在哪里找到？

transcript.text: Well, the one sector of the economy that can't be easily duplicated by even smart technologies is the caring sector, the personal care sector.
transcript.translation: 嗯，经济中一个即使智能技术也难以轻易复制的领域是关怀行业，即个人护理行业。

transcript.text: That is, you can't really get a robot to do a great massage or physical therapy, or you can't get the kind of personal attention you need with regard to therapy or any other personal service.
transcript.translation: 也就是说，你无法真正让机器人进行出色的按摩或物理治疗，或者无法在治疗或其他任何个人服务方面获得你需要的那种个人关注。

transcript.text: There could be very high-end personal services.
transcript.translation: 可能会有非常高端的个人服务。

transcript.text: Therapists do charge a lot of money.
transcript.translation: 治疗师确实收费很高。

transcript.text: I think there's no limit to the amount of personal attention and personal care people would like if they could afford it.
transcript.translation: 我认为，如果人们负担得起，他们对个人关注和护理的需求是没有上限的。

transcript.text: But the real question in the future is, how can people afford these things if they don't have money, because they can't get a job that pays enough?
transcript.translation: 但未来的真正问题是，如果人们没有钱，因为他们找不到薪水足够高的工作，他们如何负担得起这些东西？

transcript.text: That's why I wrote this book, which is about how to reorganize the economy for the future when technology brings about disruptive changes to what we used to consider high-income work.
transcript.translation: 这就是我写这本书的原因，它探讨了当技术对我们过去认为的高收入工作带来颠覆性变化时，如何为未来重组经济。

transcript.text: American researchers have discovered the world's oldest paved road, a 4,600-year-old highway.
transcript.translation: 美国研究人员发现了世界上最古老的铺砌道路，一条有4600年历史的公路。

transcript.text: It linked a stone pit in the Egyptian desert to waterways that carried blocks to monument sites along the Nile.
transcript.translation: 它连接了埃及沙漠中的一个采石场和水道，这些水道将石块运送到尼罗河沿岸的纪念碑遗址。

transcript.text: The eight-mile road is at least 500 years older than any previously discovered road.
transcript.translation: 这条八英里长的道路比任何以前发现的道路至少早500年。

transcript.text: It is the only paved road discovered in ancient Egypt, said geologist Thomas Bowne of the United States Geological Survey.
transcript.translation: 这是在古埃及发现的唯一铺砌道路，美国地质调查局的地质学家托马斯·鲍恩说。

transcript.text: He reported the discovery on Friday.
transcript.translation: 他在周五报告了这一发现。

transcript.text: The road probably doesn't rank with the pyramids as a construction feat, but it is a major engineering achievement, said his colleague, geologist James Harrell of the University of Toledo.
transcript.translation: 这条道路可能无法与金字塔的建筑壮举相提并论，但它是一项重大的工程成就，他的同事、托莱多大学的地质学家詹姆斯·哈雷尔说。

transcript.text: Not only is the road earlier than we thought possible, we didn't even think they built roads.
transcript.translation: 不仅这条道路比我们想象的要早，我们甚至没想过他们建造了道路。

transcript.text: The researchers also made a discovery in the stone pit at the northern end of the road, the first evidence that the Egyptians used rock saws.
transcript.translation: 研究人员还在道路北端的采石场有了一个发现，这是埃及人使用岩石锯的首个证据。

transcript.text: This is the oldest example of saws being used for cutting stone, said Bowne's colleague James Hoffmeyer of Wheaton College in Illinois.
transcript.translation: 这是使用锯子切割石头的最古老例子，鲍恩的同事、伊利诺伊州惠顿学院的詹姆斯·霍夫迈耶说。

transcript.text: That's two technologies we didn't know they had, Harrell said.
transcript.translation: 这是我们不知道他们拥有的两项技术，哈雷尔说。

transcript.text: And we don't know why they were both abandoned.
transcript.translation: 而且我们不知道为什么这两项技术都被放弃了。

transcript.text: The road was discovered in the Fayum Depression, about 45 miles southwest of Cairo.
transcript.translation: 这条道路是在法尤姆洼地发现的，大约在开罗西南45英里处。

transcript.text: Short segments of the road had been observed by earlier explorers, Bowne said, but they failed to realise its significance or follow up on their observations.
transcript.translation: 早期的探险家观察到了这条道路的短段，鲍恩说，但他们没有意识到它的重要性，也没有跟进他们的观察。

transcript.text: Bowne and his colleague stumbled across it while they were doing geological mapping in the region.
transcript.translation: 鲍恩和他的同事在该地区进行地质测绘时偶然发现了它。

transcript.text: The road was clearly built to provide services for the newly discovered stone pit.
transcript.translation: 这条道路显然是为了新发现的采石场提供服务而建造的。

transcript.text: Bowne and Harrell have found the camp that housed workers at the stone pit.
transcript.translation: 鲍恩和哈雷尔已经找到了安置采石场工人的营地。

transcript.text: The road appears today to go nowhere, ending in the middle of the desert.
transcript.translation: 今天看来，这条道路似乎无处可去，终止于沙漠中央。

transcript.text: When it was built, its terminal was a dock on the shore of Lake Moiris, which had an elevation of about 66 feet above sea level, the same as the dock.
transcript.translation: 当它建成时，它的终点是莫里斯湖岸上的一个码头，海拔约66英尺，与码头相同。

transcript.text: Lake Moiris received its water from the annual floods of the Nile.
transcript.translation: 莫里斯湖的水来自尼罗河的年度洪水。

transcript.text: At the time of the floods, the river and lake were at the same level and connected through a gap in the hills, near the modern villages of El Lajun and Hawara.
transcript.translation: 在洪水期间，河流和湖泊处于同一水位，并通过山中的一个缺口相连，靠近现代村庄El Lajun和Hawara。

transcript.text: Harrell and Bowne believe that blocks were loaded onto barges during the dry season, then floated over to the Nile during the floods to be shipped off to the monument sites at Giza and Saqqara.
transcript.translation: 哈雷尔和鲍恩认为，在旱季，石块被装上驳船，然后在洪水期间漂浮到尼罗河，再运送到吉萨和萨卡拉的纪念碑遗址。

transcript.text: Dr.

transcript.translation: 龚医生将它们刺入我的左臂，在一直困扰我的肘部周围。

transcript.text: Other needles were slipped into my left wrist and, strangely, into my right arm, and then into both my closed eyelids.
transcript.translation: 其他针被滑入我的左腕，奇怪的是，还刺入了我的右臂，然后是我的两个闭着的眼皮。

transcript.text: There wasn't any discomfort, just a mild warming sensation.
transcript.translation: 没有任何不适，只有一种轻微的温暖感。

transcript.text: However, I did begin to wonder what had driven me here.
transcript.translation: 然而，我开始想知道是什么驱使我来到这里。

transcript.text: To the office of Dr.
transcript.translation: 来到医生的办公室。

transcript.text: James Gong in New York's Chinatown.
transcript.translation: 位于纽约唐人街的詹姆斯·龚医生的办公室。

transcript.text: Then I remembered the torturing pain in that left elbow.
transcript.translation: 然后我想起了左肘部那折磨人的疼痛。

transcript.text: Several trips to a hospital and two expensive, uncomfortable medical tests had failed to produce even a diagnosis.
transcript.translation: 几次去医院和两次昂贵且不舒服的医疗检查都没能给出一个诊断。

transcript.text: Maybe you lean on your left arm too much, the doctor concluded, suggesting I see a bone doctor.
transcript.translation: 也许你过于依赖左臂了，医生总结道，并建议我去看骨科医生。

transcript.text: During the hours spent waiting in vain to see a bone doctor, I decided to take another track and try acupuncture.
transcript.translation: 在徒劳等待骨科医生的几个小时里，我决定换条路，尝试针灸。

transcript.text: A Chinese-American friend recommended Dr.
transcript.translation: 一位华裔朋友推荐了医生。

transcript.text: Gong.

transcript.text: I took the subway to Gong's second floor office, marked with a hand-painted sign.
transcript.translation: 我乘地铁去龚医生的二楼办公室，那里有一个手绘的招牌。

transcript.text: Dr.

transcript.text: Gong speaks English, but not often.
transcript.translation: 龚医生说英语，但不经常。

transcript.text: Most of my questions to him were greeted with a friendly laugh, but I managed to let him know where my arm hurt.
transcript.translation: 我问他大多数问题时，他都报以友好的笑声，但我还是设法让他知道我的手臂哪里疼。

transcript.text: He asked me to go into a room, had me lie down on a bed, and went to work.
transcript.translation: 他让我进一个房间，让我躺在床上，然后开始工作。

transcript.text: In the next room, I learned a woman dancer was also getting a treatment.
transcript.translation: 在隔壁房间，我得知一位女舞者也在接受治疗。

transcript.text: As I lay there a while, I drifted into a dreamlike state and fantasized about what she looked like.
transcript.translation: 我在那里躺了一会儿，进入了一种梦幻般的状态，并幻想着她的模样。

transcript.text: Acupuncturists today are as likely to be found on Park Avenue as on Mott Street.

transcript.translation: 总计，全国估计有10,000名针灸师。

transcript.text: Acupuncturists may say that the body has more than 800 acupuncture points.
transcript.translation: 针灸师可能会说身体有800多个针灸点。

transcript.text: A life force called T circulates through the body.
transcript.translation: 一种称为T的生命力在体内循环。

transcript.text: Points on the skin are energetically connected to specific organs, body structures, and systems.
transcript.translation: 皮肤上的点与特定器官、身体结构和系统有能量上的联系。

transcript.text: Acupuncture points are stimulated to balance the circulation of T.
transcript.translation: 针灸点被刺激以平衡T的循环。

transcript.text: The truth is, though, acupuncture is at least 2,200 years old.

transcript.text: Nobody really knows what's happening, says Paul Zmiewski, a Ph.

transcript.text: Ronald and Lois, married for two decades, consider themselves a happy couple, but in the early years of their marriage, both were disturbed by persistent arguments that seemed to fade away without ever being truly resolved.
transcript.translation: 罗纳德和洛伊丝结婚二十年了，他们自认为是一对幸福的夫妇，但在婚姻的早年，他们都受到持续争吵的困扰，这些争吵似乎逐渐消失，但从未真正解决。

transcript.text: They uncovered clues to what was going wrong by researching a fascinating subject, how birth order affects not only your personality, but also how compatible you are with your mate.
transcript.translation: 他们通过研究一个迷人的主题——出生顺序如何不仅影响你的个性，还影响你与伴侣的相容性——揭开了问题所在的一些线索。

transcript.text: Ronald and Lois are only children, and onlys grow up accustomed to being the apple of their parents' eyes.
transcript.translation: 罗纳德和洛伊丝都是独生子女，独生子女在成长过程中习惯于成为父母的掌上明珠。

transcript.text: Match two onlys, and you have partners who subconsciously expect each other to continue fulfilling this expectation, while neither has much experience in the giving end.
transcript.translation: 将两个独生子女配对，你得到的是一对潜意识里期望对方继续满足这种期望的伴侣，而双方在付出方面都没有太多经验。

transcript.text: Here's a list of common birth order characteristics, and some thoughts on the best, and worst, marital matches for each.
transcript.translation: 以下是一些常见的出生顺序特征，以及对每种特征的最佳和最差婚姻匹配的一些思考。

transcript.text: The oldest tends to be self-assured, responsible, a high achiever, and relatively serious and reserved.
transcript.translation: 长子往往自信、负责、成就较高，并且相对严肃和矜持。

transcript.text: He may be slow to make friends, perhaps content with only one companion.
transcript.translation: 他可能交友较慢，或许满足于只有一个伴侣。

transcript.text: The best matches are with a youngest, an only, or a mate raised in a large family.
transcript.translation: 最佳匹配是与一个幼子、独生子女或在大家庭中长大的伴侣。

transcript.text: The worst match is with another oldest, since the two will be too sovereign to share a household comfortably.
transcript.translation: 最差匹配是与另一个长子，因为两人会过于独立，难以舒适地共享一个家庭。

transcript.text: The youngest child of the family thrives on attention, and tends to be outgoing, adventurous, optimistic, creative, and less ambitious than others in the family.
transcript.translation: 家庭中的幼子在关注中茁壮成长，往往外向、爱冒险、乐观、有创造力，并且比家庭中的其他人野心较小。

transcript.text: He may lack self-discipline, and have difficulty making decisions on his own.
transcript.translation: 他可能缺乏自律，在独自做决定方面有困难。

transcript.text: A youngest brother of brothers, often unpredictable and romantic, will match best with an oldest sister of brothers.
transcript.translation: 一个兄弟中的幼弟，往往不可预测且浪漫，最适合与兄弟中的长姐匹配。

transcript.text: The youngest sister of brothers is best matched with an oldest brother of sisters, who will happily indulge these traits.
transcript.translation: 兄弟中的幼妹最适合与姐妹中的长兄匹配，后者会乐于纵容这些特质。

transcript.text: The middle child is influenced by many variables, however, middles are less likely to take initiative, and more anxious and self-critical than others.
transcript.translation: 中间子女受许多变量影响，然而，中间子女不太可能主动，并且比其他人更焦虑和自我批评。

transcript.text: Middles often successfully marry other middles, since both are strong on tact, not so strong on aggressiveness, and tend to crave affection.
transcript.translation: 中间子女经常成功地与其他中间子女结婚，因为双方都擅长策略，不那么好斗，并且渴望感情。

transcript.text: The only child is often most comfortable when alone, but since an only tends to be a well-adjusted individual, she'll eventually learn to relate to any chosen spouse.
transcript.translation: 独生子女往往在独处时最舒适，但由于独生子女往往适应良好，她最终会学会与任何选择的配偶相处。

transcript.text: The male only child expects his wife to make life easier, without getting much in return.
transcript.translation: 男性独生子女期望妻子让生活更轻松，而自己付出不多。

transcript.text: He is sometimes best matched with a younger sister of brothers.
transcript.translation: 他有时最适合与兄弟中的幼妹匹配。

transcript.text: The female only child, who tends to be slightly more flexible, is well matched with an older man, who will indulge her tendency to test his love.
transcript.translation: 女性独生子女往往更灵活一些，与年长男性匹配良好，后者会纵容她测试他爱意的倾向。

transcript.text: Her worst match?
transcript.translation: 她最差的匹配？

transcript.text: Another only, of course.
transcript.translation: 当然是另一个独生子女。

transcript.text: Questions 23 to 25 are based on the lecture you have just heard.
transcript.translation: 问题23至25基于你刚刚听到的讲座。

transcript.translation: 问题22。婚姻中最常见的出生顺序特征是什么？

questionGroups.title: Section A

paragraphs.text: When Elon Musk says that his new priority is using artificial intelligence to build domestic robots, we should look forward to the day in admiration.
paragraphs.translation: 当埃隆·马斯克说他的新重点是使用人工智能来建造家用机器人时，我们应该满怀钦佩地期待那一天的到来。

paragraphs.text: Mr. Musk is a guy who gets things done. The founder of two tech companies, Tesla Motors and SpaceX, is bringing electric vehicles to mass market and __26__ humans to live on other planets. This sounds like so much hot air, but the near $13 billion fortune this entrepreneur has __27__ comes from practical achievements rather than hypothetical ones.
paragraphs.translation: 马斯克先生是一个说到做到的人。作为两家科技公司特斯拉汽车和SpaceX的创始人，他正在将电动汽车推向大众市场，并使人类能够在其他星球上生活。这听起来像是吹牛，但这位企业家积累的近130亿美元财富来自于实际成就，而非假设。

paragraphs.text: A lot of clever people are __28__ about artificial intelligence, fearing that robots will one day become so __29__ that they'll murder all of us. These fears are mostly __30__: as with hysteria about genetic modification, we humans are generally wise enough to manage these problems with speed and care.
paragraphs.translation: 许多聪明人都对人工智能感到恐惧，担心有一天机器人会变得如此聪明以至于杀死我们所有人。这些恐惧大多是夸张的：就像对基因修改的歇斯底里一样，我们人类通常足够明智，能够快速而谨慎地处理这些问题。

paragraphs.text: And just think of how wonderful it would be if you had a live-in robot. It could, __31__, be like having a babysitter and a nurse rolled into one--or, if that required __32__ intelligence beyond the power of Mr. Musk's imagined machine, at least someone to chop the carrots, wash the car and mow the lawn. Once purchased and trained, this would allow the __33__ user to save money and time, freeing up __34__ space in our busy lives to read a good book.
paragraphs.translation: 想想看，如果你有一个住在家里机器人该多好。最终，它可能就像集保姆和护士于一身——或者，如果那需要超出马斯克先生想象的机器的能力的情感智能，至少能有人切胡萝卜、洗车和修剪草坪。一旦购买并训练好，这将使普通用户节省金钱和时间，在我们忙碌的生活中腾出宝贵的空间来读一本好书。

paragraphs.text: That is why we welcome Mr. Musk's latest __35__, and wish him well. As long as robots add to the sum of human happiness, reduce suffering, and create time to read world-class journalism, we should be their fans. Especially since journalism is one job robots will never do.
paragraphs.translation: 这就是为什么我们欢迎马斯克先生的最新项目，并祝他一切顺利。只要机器人能增加人类的总体幸福，减少痛苦，并创造时间阅读世界级的新闻报道，我们就应该成为它们的粉丝。尤其是因为新闻工作是机器人永远无法胜任的工作。

questionGroups.directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.

wordBank.meaning: 积累，聚集（amass 的过去式/过去分词）
普通的；偶然的；非正式的
使能够，使可以（enable 的现在分词）

questions.analysis: 空格在 "is bringing electric vehicles to mass market and __ humans to live on other planets" 中，与前面的 bringing 并列，需要一个 V-ing 形式作谓语；后接 "humans to live on other planets" 构成 enable sb. to do sth. 结构。eventually 是副词，无法承担动词位且不能搭配 "humans to live"，排除。语义上指马斯克在『使』人类得以在其他星球居住，故选 D enabling。
空格位于 "this entrepreneur has __" 之后接定语从句修饰 fortune，需要 has 后的过去分词构成现在完成时，且语义上需表达『积累（财富）』。amass a fortune 是固定搭配，意为聚敛巨额财富。故选 A amassed。

空格在 "are __ about artificial intelligence, fearing that..." 中，需 be + 形容词，描述人对 AI 的情绪状态；下文 fearing that robots will... murder all of us 进一步说明这种情绪是『害怕』。terrified 与 about 搭配，意为对某事极度恐惧，与 fearing 语义呼应。故选 N terrified。
空格在 "become so __ that they'll murder all of us" 中，so...that 结构需要形容词；语义上指机器人变得非常聪明、聪明到反过来威胁人类。terrified 已用于 28 题且语义不符；smart 直接对应 AI 的智能程度。故选 L smart。
空格在 "These fears are mostly __" 中，be + adv. + 形容词构成系表，需要形容词；冒号后说明人类有能力管理这些问题，暗示前面的恐惧是言过其实。misleading 强调误导性，但作者重点是恐惧『被夸大』，而非『误导他人』。故选 F exaggerated。
空格被两个逗号隔开作插入语："It could, __, be like having a babysitter and a nurse rolled into one"，插入语位置最常见是副词。enabling 是动词形式，无法作插入语；语义上说『最终』机器人能集保姆与护士于一身，承接前文 "if you had a live-in robot" 的设想。故选 E eventually。
空格修饰名词 intelligence，需要形容词。原文设想机器人当『保姆+护士』，但承认这需要某种『超出马斯克所设想机器能力』的智能 —— 与照护、陪伴最直接相关的是 emotional intelligence（情商），是英语中固定搭配。extravagant intelligence 不通顺。故选 C emotional。
空格在 "allow the __ user to save money and time" 中，前 the 后 user，必须填形容词修饰 user。generously 是副词，不能作定语。语义上指普通的、非专业的家用机器人使用者得以省时省钱。故选 B casual。
空格修饰名词 space，需形容词；上文谈到节省金钱与时间，下文说『腾出空间来读好书』，说明这空间是宝贵稀缺的。故选 J precious。
空格在 "Mr. Musk's latest __" 中，需名词作 latest 的中心词；全文围绕马斯克新涉足家用机器人这一新事业（business venture），与开篇 "his new priority" 呼应。reward / sphere 与 latest 搭配语义不通。故选 O venture。

questionGroups.title: In the real world, nobody cares that you went to an Ivy League school

material.title: In the real world, nobody cares that you went to an Ivy League school

paragraphs.text: As a high school junior, everything in my life revolved around getting into the right college. I diligently attended my SAT, ACT, and Advanced Placement test preparation courses. I juggled cross-country and track schedules, newspaper staff, and my church's youth group and drama team. I didn't drink, party, or even do much dating. The right college, I thought, was one with prestige, one with a name. It didn't have to be the Ivy League, but it needed to be "top school."
paragraphs.translation: 作为一名高中三年级学生，我生活中的一切都围绕着进入理想的大学。我勤奋地参加SAT、ACT和AP考试准备课程。我兼顾越野跑和田径训练、报社工作，以及教会的青年小组和戏剧团队。我不喝酒、不参加派对，甚至很少约会。我认为理想的大学应该是有声望、有名气的。它不一定是常春藤联盟，但必须是“顶尖学校”。

paragraphs.text: Looking back now, nine years later, I can't remember exactly what it was about these universities that made them seem so much better. Was it a curriculum that appeared more rigorous, perhaps? Or an alumni network that I hoped would open doors down the line? Maybe. "I do think there are advantages to schools with more recognition," notes Marybeth Gasman, a professor of higher education at the University of Pennsylvania. "I don't necessarily think that's a reason to go to one."
paragraphs.translation: 如今，九年过去了，我无法准确记得这些大学究竟为何显得如此优秀。也许是课程看起来更严谨？或者是我期望校友网络能为未来打开大门？也许吧。“我确实认为知名学校有其优势，”宾夕法尼亚大学高等教育教授Marybeth Gasman指出。“但这不一定是选择它们的理由。”

paragraphs.text: In reflection, my firm belief in the power of the brand was naive, not to mention a bit snobby. I quickly passed over state schools and southern schools, believing their curriculum to be automatically inferior to northeastern or western counterparts. Instead, I dreamed of living in New York City and my parents obliged me with a visit to New York University's (NYU) campus. During the tour, tuition fees were discussed. (NYU is consistently ranked one of the country's most expensive schools, with room and board costs totaling upwards of $64,000 a year.) Up until then, I hadn't truly realized just how expensive an education can be. Over the next few months, I realized not only could I not afford my dream school, I couldn't even afford the ones where I'd been accepted. City University of New York (CUNY), Rutgers University, and Indiana University were out of reach as were Mississippi State and the University of Alabama, where I would have to pay out-of-state fees. Further complicating my college search was a flourishing stack career—I wanted to keep running but my times weren't quite fast enough to secure a scholarship.
paragraphs.translation: 回想起来，我曾坚定相信品牌的力量，这很天真，更不用说有点势利了。我迅速忽略了州立学校和南方学校，认为它们的课程自动不如东北部或西部的学校。相反，我梦想着住在纽约市，父母便带我参观了纽约大学（NYU）校园。在参观过程中，讨论了学费问题。（NYU一直被列为全国最昂贵的学校之一，食宿费用每年高达64,000美元以上。）直到那时，我才真正意识到教育可以如此昂贵。在接下来的几个月里，我不仅负担不起梦想中的学校，甚至负担不起已经录取我的学校。纽约城市大学（CUNY）、罗格斯大学和印第安纳大学遥不可及，密西西比州立大学和阿拉巴马大学也是如此，因为我需要支付州外学费。更复杂的是，我有一段蓬勃发展的田径生涯——我想继续跑步，但成绩不够快，无法获得奖学金。

paragraphs.text: And so, at 11pm on the night of Georgia State University's (GSU) midnight deadline, I applied online. Rated No.466 overall on Forbes' Lists Top Colleges, No. 183 in Research Universities, and No. 108 in the South, I can't say it was my top choice. Still, the track coach had offered me a walk-on spot, and I actually found the urban Atlanta campus a decent consolation prize after New York City.
paragraphs.translation: 于是，在乔治亚州立大学（GSU）午夜截止日期的晚上11点，我在线提交了申请。它在福布斯顶级大学榜单上总体排名第466位，研究型大学排名第183位，南方大学排名第108位，我不能说它是首选。尽管如此，田径教练给了我一个试训名额，而且我发现在亚特兰大市区的校园在纽约之后算是不错的安慰奖。

paragraphs.text: While it may have been practical, it wasn't prestigious, But here's the thing: I loved my "lower-tier" university. (I use the term "low-tier" cautiously, because GSU is a well-regarded research institution that attracts high quality professors and faculty from all over the country.) We are taught to believe that only by going to the best schools and getting the best grades can we escape the rat race and build a better future. But what if lower-tier colleges and universities were the ticket to escaping the rat race? After all, where else can you leave school with a decent degree—but without a lifetime of debt?
paragraphs.translation: 虽然它可能很实用，但不够知名。但问题是：我爱我的“低层”大学。（我谨慎使用“低层”一词，因为GSU是一所备受尊敬的研究机构，吸引了全国的高质量教授和教员。）我们被教导相信，只有进入最好的学校、取得最好的成绩，才能逃离激烈竞争，创造更美好的未来。但如果低层院校正是逃离激烈竞争的途径呢？毕竟，哪里还能让你带着一个不错的学位离开学校，却不用背负一生的债务？

paragraphs.text: My school didn't come pre-packaged like the more popular options, so we were left to take care of ourselves, figuring out city life and trying to complete degree programs that no one was championing for us to succeed in. What I'm saying is, I loved my university because it taught us all to be resourceful and we could make what we wanted out of it.
paragraphs.translation: 我的学校不像更受欢迎的选项那样预先包装好，所以我们需要自己照顾自己，摸索城市生活，并努力完成那些没人会为我们加油助威的学位课程。我想说的是，我爱我的大学，因为它教会了我们所有人随机应变，我们可以从中创造自己想要的东西。

paragraphs.text: I was lucky enough to have my tuition covered by a lottery-funded scholarship called HOPE (Helping Outstanding Pupils Educationally) When I started college, the HOPE scholarship was funded by the state of Georgia and offered to graduating high school seniors with a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Living costs and books I paid for with money earned during high school, supplemented by a small college fund my deceased grandfather left for me and a modest savings account my parents created when I was born.
paragraphs.translation: 我很幸运，学费由一个名为HOPE（教育资助优秀学生）的彩票资助奖学金覆盖。当我开始上大学时，HOPE奖学金由乔治亚州资助，提供给高中毕业、GPA在3.0或以上的学生。生活费和书本费我用高中期间赚的钱支付，并补充了已故祖父留给我的一小笔大学基金和我父母在我出生时创建的 modest 储蓄账户。

paragraphs.text: So what about all that name recognition? Sure, many of my colleagues and competitors have more glamorous alma maters than I do. As a journalist, I have competed against NYU, Columbia, and Northeastern graduates for jobs. And yet, not a single interviewer has ever asked me about my educational background. In fact, almost every interview I've ever had was due to a connection—one that I've gained through pure determination, not a school brand.
paragraphs.translation: 那么，所有这些名气有什么用呢？当然，我的许多同事和竞争对手都有比我更光鲜的母校。作为一名记者，我曾与NYU、哥伦比亚大学和东北大学的毕业生竞争工作。然而，没有一个面试官问过我的教育背景。事实上，我几乎每一次面试都是由于人脉——那是通过纯粹的决心获得的，而不是学校品牌。

paragraphs.text: According to The Boston Globe, students who earned their bachelor's in 2012 have an average monthly loan payment of $312, which is one-third more than those who graduated in 2004. Ultimately, that's the thing universities don't want to admit. Private universities are money-making institutions. If you can afford to buy prestige, that's your choice. For the rest of us, however, our hearty lower-tiered universities are just fine, thank you.
paragraphs.translation: 据《波士顿环球报》报道，2012年获得学士学位的学生平均每月贷款还款为312美元，比2004年毕业的学生多出三分之一。归根结底，这是大学不愿承认的事情。私立大学是赚钱的机构。如果你能买得起名声，那是你的选择。但对我们其余人来说，我们热心的低层大学就很好了，谢谢。

paragraphs.text: Wealthy universities talk up the benefits their name will give graduates; namely, strong alumni networks, star faculty, and a résumé boost. But you needn't attend an Ivy League school to reap those rewards. Ludacris and the former CEO of Bank of America Ken Lewis are alumni of my college, as well as VICE's first female editor-in-chief, Ellis Jones. Successful people tend to be successful no matter where they go to school. And lower-tier schools can have alumni networks just as strong as their big name counterparts. In fact, lower-tier school alumni networks are arguably stronger, because fellow alumni recognize that you didn't necessarily have an easy path to follow. They might be more willing to offer career help, because your less famous school denotes that, like them., you are also full of energy and perseverance.
paragraphs.translation: 富裕的大学夸耀其名称将给毕业生带来的好处；即强大的校友网络、明星教师和简历加分。但你不需要上常春藤学校才能获得这些回报。Ludacris和美国银行前首席执行官Ken Lewis是我的大学校友，还有VICE的第一位女主编Ellis Jones。成功人士往往无论在哪里上学都会成功。低层学校可以拥有与知名学校一样强大的校友网络。事实上，低层学校的校友网络可能更强，因为校友们意识到你不一定有一条容易的路要走。他们可能更愿意提供职业帮助，因为你不那么出名的学校表明，像他们一样，你也充满活力和毅力。

paragraphs.text: The Washington Post reported on a recent study by Princeton economists, in which college graduates, who applied to the most selective schools in the 12th grade were compared to those who applied to slightly less selective schools. They found that students with more potential earned more as adults, and the reverse held true as well, no matter where they went to school.
paragraphs.translation: 《华盛顿邮报》报道了普林斯顿经济学家最近的一项研究，其中将12年级申请了最具选择性学校的大学毕业生与申请了选择性稍低学校的毕业生进行了比较。他们发现，潜力更大的学生在成年后收入更高，反之亦然，无论他们在哪里上学。

paragraphs.text: Likewise, star faculty is not always found where you'd expect. Big name schools are not necessarily the best places for professors; plus, many professors split teaching time between multiple colleges and/or universities. This means, for instance, a CUNY student could reasonably expect to receive the same quality of instruction from a prestigious professor as they would if they were enrolled in the same class at NYU.
paragraphs.translation: 同样，明星教师并不总是在你期望的地方。名牌学校不一定是教授的最佳去处；此外，许多教授在多个学院和/或大学之间分配教学时间。这意味着，例如，CUNY学生可以合理地期望从一位知名教授那里获得与在NYU注册同一课程相同的教学质量。

paragraphs.text: It's possible that some hiring managers may be drawn to candidates with a particular educational résumé, but it's no guarantee. According to a 2012 survey described in The Atlantic, college reputation ranked lowest in relative importance of attributes in evaluating graduates for hire, beaten out by top factors like internships, employment during college, college major, volunteer experience, and extracurriculars.
paragraphs.translation: 一些招聘经理可能被具有特定教育简历的候选人吸引，但这没有保证。根据《大西洋月刊》描述的一项2012年调查，大学声誉在评估毕业生雇佣的属性相对重要性中排名最低，被实习、大学期间就业、大学专业、志愿者经历和课外活动等顶级因素超越。

paragraphs.text: Maybe students who choose less prestigious universities are bound to succeed because they are determined to. I tend to think so. In any case, if I could do it again, I'd still make the same choice. Today I'm debt-free, resourceful—and I understand that even the shiniest packaging can't predict what you'll find on the inside.
paragraphs.translation: 也许选择不太知名大学的学生注定会成功，因为他们决心如此。我倾向于这样认为。无论如何，如果重来一次，我仍会做出同样的选择。今天，我无债一身轻，足智多谋——我明白即使最闪亮的包装也无法预测内在的东西。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Economically speaking, are we better off than we were ten years ago? Twenty years ago? In their thirst for evidence on this issue, commentators seized on the recent report by the Census Bureau, which found that average household income rose by 5.2% in 2015.
paragraphs.translation: 从经济角度看，我们比十年前更富裕吗？比二十年前呢？评论家们渴望获得这个问题的证据，因此抓住了人口普查局最近的一份报告，该报告发现2015年平均家庭收入增长了5.2%。

paragraphs.text: Unfortunately, that conclusion puts too much weight on a useful, but flawed and incomplete, statistic. Among the more significant problems with the Census's measure are that: 1) it excludes taxes, transfers, and compensation like employer-provided health insurance; and 2) it is based on surveys rather than data. Even if precisely measured, income data exclude important determinants of economic well-being, such as the hours of work needed to earn that income.
paragraphs.translation: 不幸的是，这一结论过于依赖一个有用但有缺陷且不完整的统计指标。人口普查局衡量方法中较为重要的问题包括：1) 它排除了税收、转移支付和雇主提供的健康保险等补偿；2) 它基于调查而非数据。即使精确测量，收入数据也排除了经济福祉的重要决定因素，例如赚取该收入所需的工作时长。

paragraphs.text: While thinking about the question, we came across a recently published article by Charles Jones and Peter Klenow, which proposes an interesting new measure of economic welfare. While by no means perfect, it is considerably more comprehensive than average income, taking into account not only growth in consumption per person but also changes in working time, life expectancy, and inequality. Moreover, it can be used to assess economic performance both across countries and over time.
paragraphs.translation: 在思考这个问题时，我们偶然发现查尔斯·琼斯和彼得·克伦诺最近发表的一篇文章，该文章提出了一种有趣的新经济福利衡量方法。尽管绝非完美，但它比平均收入全面得多，不仅考虑了人均消费的增长，还考虑了工作时间、预期寿命和不平等的变化。此外，它可以用于评估跨国和跨时间的经济表现。

paragraphs.text: The Jones-Klenow method can be illustrated by a cross-country example. Suppose we want to compare the economic welfare of citizens of the U.S. and France in 2005.
paragraphs.translation: 琼斯-克伦诺方法可以通过一个跨国示例来说明。假设我们想比较2005年美国和法国公民的经济福利。

paragraphs.text: In 2005, as the authors observe, real consumption per person in France was only 60% as high as in the U.S., making it appear that Americans were economically much better off than the French on average. However, that comparison omits other relevant factors: leisure time, life expectancy, and economic inequality. The French take longer vacations and retire earlier, so typically work fewer hours; they enjoy a higher life expectancy, presumably reflecting advantages with respect to health care, diet, lifestyle, and the like; and income and consumption are somewhat more equally distributed there than in the U.S. Because of these differences, comparing France's consumption with the U.S.'s overstates the gap in economic welfare.
paragraphs.translation: 正如作者所观察到的，2005年法国的实际人均消费仅为美国的60%，这似乎表明美国人在经济上平均比法国人富裕得多。然而，这一比较忽略了其他相关因素：休闲时间、预期寿命和经济不平等。法国人休假更长，退休更早，因此通常工作时间更短；他们享有更高的预期寿命，可能反映了在医疗保健、饮食、生活方式等方面的优势；而且法国的收入和消费分配比美国更平等。由于这些差异，将法国的消费与美国比较夸大了经济福利的差距。

paragraphs.text: Similar calculations can be used to compare the U.S. and other countries. For example, this calculation puts economic welfare in the United Kingdom at 97% of U.S. levels, but estimates Mexican well-being at 22%.
paragraphs.translation: 类似的计算可用于比较美国和其他国家。例如，这一计算将英国的经济福利定为美国水平的97%，但估计墨西哥的福祉为22%。

paragraphs.text: The Jones-Klenow measure can also assess an economy's performance over time. According to this measure, as of the early-to-mid-2000s, the U.S. had the highest economic welfare of any large country. Since 2007, economic welfare in the U.S. has continued to improve. However, the pace of improvement has slowed markedly.
paragraphs.translation: 琼斯-克伦诺衡量方法还可以评估一个经济体随时间的表现。根据这一衡量方法，截至21世纪初至中期，美国是所有大型国家中经济福利最高的。自2007年以来，美国的经济福利持续改善。然而，改善的速度已明显放缓。

paragraphs.text: Methodologically, the lesson from the Jones-Klenow research is that economic welfare is multi-dimensional. Their approach is flexible enough that in principle other important quality-of-life changes could be incorporated—for example, decreases in total emissions of pollutants and declines in crime rates.
paragraphs.translation: 从方法论上看，琼斯-克伦诺研究的启示是经济福利是多维度的。他们的方法足够灵活，原则上可以纳入其他重要的生活质量变化——例如，污染物总排放量的减少和犯罪率的下降。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: If you've ever started a sentence with, "If I were you..." or found yourself scratching your head at a colleague's agony over a decision when the answer is crystal-clear, there's a scientific reason behind it. Our own decision-making abilities can become depleted over the course of the day causing indecision or poor choices, but choosing on behalf of someone else is an enjoyable task that doesn't suffer the same pitfalls.
paragraphs.translation: 如果你曾经以'如果我是你……'开头说一句话，或者发现同事在答案显而易见的情况下为决定而苦恼时感到困惑，这背后有科学原因。我们自己的决策能力在一天中会逐渐耗尽，导致犹豫不决或做出糟糕的选择，但为别人做选择却是一项愉快的任务，不会受到同样的陷阱影响。

paragraphs.text: The problem is "decision fatigue," a psychological phenomenon that takes a toll on the quality of your choices after a long day of decision making, says Evan Polman, a leading psychologist.
paragraphs.translation: 心理学家Evan Polman说，问题是'决策疲劳'，这是一种心理现象，在一天漫长的决策后会影响选择的质量。

paragraphs.text: Physicians who have been on the job for several hours, for example, are more likely to prescribe antibiotics to patients when it's unwise to do so. "Presumably it's because it's simple and easy to write a prescription and consider a patient case closed rather than investigate further," Polman says.
paragraphs.translation: 例如，工作几个小时的医生更有可能在不明智的情况下给患者开抗生素。Polman说：'可能是因为开处方并认为患者病例结束比进一步调查更简单容易。'

paragraphs.text: But decision fatigue goes away when you are making the decision for someone else. When people imagine themselves as advisers and imagine their own choices as belonging to someone else, they feel less tired and rely less on decision shortcuts to make those choices. "By taking upon the role of adviser rather than decision maker, one does not suffer the consequences of decision fatigue," he says. "It is as if there is something fun and liberating about making someone else's choice."
paragraphs.translation: 但当你为别人做决定时，决策疲劳会消失。当人们想象自己是顾问，并将自己的选择视为属于别人时，他们感觉不那么累，并且更少依赖决策捷径来做出这些选择。他说：'通过扮演顾问而不是决策者的角色，人们不会承受决策疲劳的后果。这就好像为别人做选择有一种有趣和解放的感觉。'

paragraphs.text: Getting input from others not only offers a fresh perspective and thought process, it often also includes riskier choices. While this sounds undesirable, it can be quite good, says Polman. "when people experience decision fatigue-when they are tired of making choices-they have a tendency to choose to go with status quo," he says. "But the status quo can be problematic. Since a change in the course of action can sometimes be important and lead to a positive outcome."
paragraphs.translation: 从他人那里获取输入不仅提供了新的视角和思维过程，通常还包括更冒险的选择。Polman说，虽然这听起来不理想，但它可能相当好。他说：'当人们经历决策疲劳——当他们厌倦了做选择时——他们倾向于选择维持现状。但现状可能有问题，因为行动过程的改变有时很重要，并可能导致积极的结果。'

paragraphs.text: In order to achieve a successful outcome or reward, some level of risk is almost always essential. "People who are susceptible to decision fatigue will likely choose to do nothing over something," he says. "That's not to say that risk is always good, but it is related to taking action, whereas decision fatigue assuredly leads to inaction and the possible chagrin of a decision maker who might otherwise prefer a new course but is unfortunately hindered."
paragraphs.translation: 为了获得成功的结果或回报，某种程度的风险几乎总是必不可少的。他说：'容易决策疲劳的人可能会选择什么都不做，而不是采取行动。这并不是说风险总是好的，但它与采取行动有关，而决策疲劳肯定会导致不作为，以及决策者可能本倾向于新方向但不幸受阻的可能懊恼。'

paragraphs.text: Just because you can make good choices for others doesn't mean you'll do the same for yourself, polman cautions. "Research has found that women negotiate higher salaries for others than they do for themselves," he says, adding that people slip in and out of decision roles.
paragraphs.translation: Polman警告说，你能为别人做出好选择并不意味着你也能为自己这样做。他说：'研究发现，女性为他人谈判的薪水比为自己谈判的要高，'并补充说，人们会滑入和滑出决策角色。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What does the author say about people making decisions?

options.label: A
options.text: They may become exhausted by making too many decisions for themselves.

options.label: B
options.text: They are more cautious in making decisions for others than for themselves.

options.label: C
options.text: They tend to make decisions the way they think advantageous to them.

options.label: D
options.text: They show considerable differences in their decision-making abilities.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第一段提到'Our own decision-making abilities can become depleted over the course of the day causing indecision or poor choices'，说明人们在一天中做太多决策后可能会感到疲惫。因此A选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: 'They are more cautious in making decisions for others than for themselves'与文章内容不符，文章指出为他人做决策时不会感到疲劳
wrongOptions.C: 'They tend to make decisions the way they think advantageous to them'未在文章中提及，文章讨论的是决策疲劳现象
wrongOptions.D: 'They show considerable differences in their decision-making abilities'也未在文章中提及，文章强调的是决策疲劳对决策能力的影响

questions.questionText: What does the example about the physicians illustrate?

options.label: A
options.text: Patients seldom receive due care towards the end of the day.

options.label: B
options.text: Prescription of antibiotics can be harmful to patients'health.

options.label: C
options.text: Decision fatigue may prevent people making wise decisions.

options.label: D
options.text: Medical doctors are especially susceptible to decision fatigue.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第二段提到'Physicians who have been on the job for several hours, for example, are more likely to prescribe antibiotics to patients when it's unwise to do so'，说明决策疲劳可能导致人们做出不明智的决策。因此C选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'Patients seldom receive due care towards the end of the day'文章未提及，仅以医生为例说明决策疲劳现象
wrongOptions.B: 'Prescription of antibiotics can be harmful to patients'health'虽然提到了不明智的处方，但并非文章讨论的重点
wrongOptions.D: 'Medical doctors are especially susceptible to decision fatigue'文章未提及医生特别容易受到决策疲劳的影响，而是以医生为例说明决策疲劳

questions.questionText: When do people feel less decision fatigue?

options.label: A
options.text: When they take decision shortcuts.

options.label: B
options.text: When they help others to make decisions.

options.label: C
options.text: When they have major decisions to make.

options.label: D
options.text: When they have advisers to turn to.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第三段提到'But decision fatigue goes away when you are making the decision for someone else'，说明当人们帮助他人做决策时，会感到较少的决策疲劳。因此B选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'When they take decision shortcuts'文章中提到依赖决策捷径是决策疲劳的表现，而非减少决策疲劳的方法
wrongOptions.C: 'When they have major decisions to make'与文章内容相反，文章指出决策疲劳会导致人们不愿做重大决策
wrongOptions.D: 'When they have advisers to turn to'文章未提及顾问对减少决策疲劳的影响

questions.questionText: What are people likely to do when decision fatigue sets in?

options.label: A
options.text: They turn to physicians for advice.

options.label: B
options.text: They tend to make risky decisions.

options.label: C
options.text: They adopt a totally new perspective.

options.label: D
options.text: They refrain from trying anything new.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第四段提到'when people experience decision fatigue-when they are tired of making choices-they have a tendency to choose to go with status quo'，说明当决策疲劳发生时，人们倾向于不尝试新事物，维持现状。因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'They turn to physicians for advice'文章未提及人们在决策疲劳时会向医生寻求建议
wrongOptions.B: 'They tend to make risky decisions'与文章内容相反，文章指出决策疲劳时人们倾向于选择现状而非冒险
wrongOptions.C: 'They adopt a totally new perspective'文章未提及人们在决策疲劳时会采取全新的视角

questions.questionText: What does the passage say about taking some risk in decision making?

options.label: A
options.text: It is vital for one to reach the goal desired.

options.label: B
options.text: It is likely to entail serious consequences.

options.label: C
options.text: It will enable people to be more creative.

options.label: D
options.text: It will more often than not end in regret.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章最后一段提到'In order to achieve a successful outcome or reward, some level of risk is almost always essential'，说明在决策中承担一定风险对于实现目标至关重要。因此A选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: 'It is likely to entail serious consequences'文章未提及风险决策可能带来的严重后果
wrongOptions.C: 'It will enable people to be more creative'文章未提及风险决策能够激发人们的创造力
wrongOptions.D: 'It will more often than not end in regret'与文章内容相反，文章指出决策疲劳导致不采取行动可能带来遗憾

questionGroups.sourceText: 自行车曾经是中国城乡最主要的交通工具,中国一度被称为"自行车王国"。如今,随着城市交通拥堵和空气污染日益严重,骑自行车又开始起来。近来,中国企业家将移动互联网技术与传统自行车结合在一起,发明了一种称为共享单车 (shared bikes) 的商业模式。共享单车的出现使骑车出行更加方便,人们仅需一部手机就可以随时使用共享单车。为了鼓励人们骑车出行,很多城市修建了自行车道。现在,越来越多的中国人也喜欢通过骑车健身。

answer.modelTranslation: Bicycles were once the primary mode of transportation in both urban and rural areas of China, and the country was once known as the 'Kingdom of Bicycles'. Nowadays, with increasing urban traffic congestion and air pollution, cycling has made a comeback. Recently, Chinese entrepreneurs have combined mobile internet technology with traditional bicycles to invent a business model known as shared bikes. The emergence of shared bikes has made cycling more convenient, as people can use them anytime with just a smartphone. To encourage cycling, many cities have built bicycle lanes. Nowadays, an increasing number of Chinese people also enjoy fitness through cycling.
translationNotes: 注意'曾经是'的翻译，可用were once或used to be表达
'一度被称为'可译为was once known as或was referred to as
'日益严重'译为increasing或growing，注意与'严重'搭配的副词使用
'商业模式'译为business model，注意model的使用
'使...更加方便'可译为make more convenient或facilitate
'仅需'可译为just need或only need，注意与'一部手机'搭配
'修建'可译为build或construct，注意与'自行车道'搭配
'越来越多的'可译为an increasing number of或more and more，注意与'中国人'搭配
'喜欢通过...健身'可译为enjoy fitness through或like to exercise by，注意与'骑车'搭配
scoringPoints: 准确翻译'曾经是'和'一度被称为'的表达
时态使用恰当，注意过去时和现在时的区分
词汇选择准确(congestion, pollution, convenient等)
固定搭配使用得当(Kingdom of Bicycles, mobile internet technology等)
句子结构完整流畅，注意主从句的使用
地道表达的使用(make a comeback, enjoy fitness through等)
